clue.text: I'd easily get nth term in integration wrong: I might need to work on calculus

definitions.text: I might need to work on calculus

indicators.note: letters that come out wrong are in the wrong order and must be put right
a term is an end or limit, so only the closing letter of the next word is kept

parts.note: the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A maths student frets that calculus will trip them up when integrating to the nth term.
explanation.walkthrough: Calculus is not maths here: it is the hard tartar on teeth, which a DENTAL HYGIENIST scrapes off.
explanation.definitionFit: Calculus is also the dental name for tartar, and removing tartar deposits from teeth is the hygienist's job.

clue.text: Letter at back of The Times in the morning paper

indicators.note: one piece sits within the other, so it is put inside
the letter standing at the back of a word is its last one

explanation.surface: Something about the final letter printed on the back of The Times, a morning newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: The Times looks like the newspaper, but it is the multiplication sign; E and X together sit in the morning.
explanation.definitionFit: A paper is a written test sat by students, as in an examination question paper.

clue.text: Review what rustler might do?

definitions.meaning: second meaning, read literally: a cattle thief carries off livestock

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase normally means to pause and assess; the question mark flags the literal reading, since stock is farm animals.
explanation.definitionFit: To take stock is an idiom for pausing to assess, and literally describes a thief stealing farm cattle.

clue.text: Tense between two cities around this time

indicators.note: something placed between two others is enclosed by them

parts.note: LA, Los Angeles, and Ely, a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire

explanation.surface: A nervous moment caught between two cities at about the present time.
explanation.walkthrough: Tense looks like an adjective for nerves; it is the grammar abbreviation. Ely is a small English cathedral city.
explanation.definitionFit: Lately means recently, in the period close to now, so roughly at the present time.

clue.text: Frank to pull up outside Tom's after getting lost

indicators.note: one piece goes around the outside of the other

parts.note: to pull up a car is to stop and park it

indicators.note: something that has got lost has gone astray, so the letters wander into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone frank wants to pull up outside Tom's house after getting lost on the way.
explanation.walkthrough: Frank looks like an honest person, but it is a verb: to stamp a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To frank a letter is to stamp it with an official mark showing postage paid, which is to postmark it.

clue.text: Out with family for spin

parts.note: news that is out is known to everyone

explanation.surface: Going out with the family for a spin in the car.
explanation.walkthrough: A spin suggests a drive, but here it is the media sense of presenting things favourably.
explanation.definitionFit: Spin is slanted presentation of news to look good, which is the craft of a press and image department.

clue.text: Tricks and blues regularly seen during shows

indicators.note: something seen during an event appears within it, so it goes inside

parts.note: sights are spectacles, things on show

indicators.note: at regular intervals, so every other letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: Tricks and blues music performed at concerts.
explanation.walkthrough: Sleight is the deft handling of a conjuror, as in sleight of hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleights are deceptive feats of dexterity, the deceptions a magician performs to fool an audience.

clue.text: Mum with the others bedding husband that's virile

indicators.note: to bed something is to tuck it in, so one piece is enclosed

parts.note: as in 'and Co', meaning and the rest

explanation.surface: Mum and the others put a husband to bed, the virile type.
explanation.definitionFit: Macho describes aggressively masculine behaviour, a show of strength and manliness.

clue.text: Vibrating as ringtone going off

indicators.note: something going off is exploding or going bad, so the letters are scattered

explanation.surface: A phone buzzing in the pocket as its ringtone sounds.
explanation.definitionFit: To resonate is to vibrate in sympathy, producing a deep sustained sound.

clue.text: Rubbish out of sight behind a bin at the front across street

parts.note: behind one's back, where one cannot see

indicators.note: only the letter standing at the front of the word is used

explanation.surface: Rubbish left out of sight behind the bins at the front of a house across the street.
explanation.walkthrough: Rubbish looks like a noun for litter, but it is a verb: to criticise. 'Across' places the a-and-b pair on the far side of the street abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: To rubbish someone is to disparage them, and to backstab is to disparage or betray them treacherously when they are absent.

clue.text: Provide cover for nurse with patient

parts.note: Enrolled Nurse, a former British nursing grade
doctors speak of a patient as a case

explanation.surface: Arranging for someone to stand in for a nurse who is with a patient.
explanation.walkthrough: Provide cover suggests standing in for a colleague; here it means wrapping something up.
explanation.definitionFit: To encase is to enclose something in a casing, physically surrounding it with a protective covering.

clue.text: Opening tills when busy is good thing for customers

indicators.note: a busy scene is all bustle and disorder, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A shop opening extra tills at a busy time is a boon for shoppers.
explanation.definitionFit: A selling point is a feature of a product that attracts buyers, an advantage for the shopper.

clue.text: You shouldn't have one club covering back for sex worker on street?

indicators.note: the outer pieces cover the inner one by sitting on either side

parts.note: ta is British slang for thanks, as said on receiving a gift

indicators.note: the back of a word is its last letter, so only that is used

parts.note: a driver is a golf club

explanation.surface: A warning against one club employing a sex worker on the street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sex worker' reads as one phrase; split it, as sex is only wordplay and the definition is the worker on the street.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabbie spends the working day out on the roads, so is literally a worker on the street, with a question mark for the joke.

clue.text: House provides wall for a large circular light

indicators.note: a wall encloses what is inside, so one piece goes around the others

explanation.surface: A house that has a wall built for a big round lamp.
explanation.definitionFit: A halo is a ring of light, such as around the moon or a saint's head in paintings.

clue.text: Turning devices and tech off getting overwhelmed by crap

indicators.note: to be overwhelmed is to be swamped and surrounded, so one piece goes inside
something that is off is wrong or spoiled, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Tools and gadgets switched off and swamped by junk.
explanation.walkthrough: Crap looks like a noun for junk; it is an exclamation, like 'Rats!'.
explanation.definitionFit: A ratchet is a toothed mechanism allowing rotation in one direction only, used in turning tools like socket wrenches.

clue.text: See 1 Across
US novelist to live in place south of California

parts.note: to dwell is to reside somewhere

explanation.surface: An American writer choosing to live somewhere south of California.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, south of means below, so the second piece comes after the first.
explanation.definitionFit: Erskine Caldwell was an American author, best known for Tobacco Road and God's Little Acre.

clue.text: Children's game a bit of fun before party

parts.note: a kick is a thrill, as in doing something for kicks

explanation.surface: A playground game is a bit of fun before the party starts.
explanation.definitionFit: Kickball is a playground sport like baseball, played by kicking a rubber ball instead of hitting it.

clue.text: Joke entertaining northern crowd

indicators.note: to entertain a guest is to take them in, so one piece holds the other

explanation.surface: A joke that amuses a crowd in the north of England.
explanation.definitionFit: A gang is a group of people who associate together, a set or crowd of friends.

clue.text: Surviving as tooth bites leg

indicators.note: teeth that bite close around something, holding it inside

parts.note: a cog is a tooth on a gear wheel

explanation.surface: A wounded person survives being bitten on the leg.
explanation.walkthrough: Tooth looks like part of a mouth; it is a gear tooth.
explanation.definitionFit: Coping means managing a difficult situation successfully, getting by, which is surviving it.

clue.text: Tennis shot is good to go past Pat

parts.note: to round a corner is to go past it
to pat an animal is to stroke it

explanation.surface: A tennis player called Pat hits a shot that is good enough to get past.
explanation.walkthrough: Pat looks like a player's name; it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A groundstroke is a tennis shot played after the ball has bounced, such as a forehand or backhand.

clue.text: Inappropriate of you to sleep with escort, ultimately

parts.note: a nap is a short sleep

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter is used

explanation.surface: It is improper of you to end up sleeping with an escort.
explanation.definitionFit: Unapt means unsuitable or not fitting, so not appropriate for the occasion.

clue.text: Drink around villa on vacation

indicators.note: vacated means emptied, so the inside of the word is cleared out leaving its ends

explanation.surface: Drinks served around a holiday villa.
explanation.definitionFit: Cava is a sparkling white wine from Spain, an alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Fly from gate that's not opened through cuts

indicators.note: a word that is not opened has lost its opening, its first letter
something that cuts into another is placed inside it

parts.note: the word without its first letter

explanation.surface: Taking a flight from an airport gate that has not opened because of staff cuts.
explanation.walkthrough: Gate and cuts suggest an airport strike; the gate merely loses its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To aviate is to pilot or travel in an aircraft, the formal verb for flying.

clue.text: Genuine tailoring with front cut out needing alteration

indicators.note: cutting out the front removes the first letter of the word
something needing alteration must be changed, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the word without its first letter

explanation.surface: Authentic tailoring with the front panel cut out, which now needs alteration.
explanation.walkthrough: Tailoring and alteration point to a dressmaker; both are wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Original means authentic, not a copy or imitation, so genuine in the sense of real.

clue.text: Prince shakes and talks nonsense

parts.note: to rattle is to shake noisily

explanation.surface: A prince trembles and babbles foolishly.
explanation.definitionFit: To prattle is to chatter at length in a childish or foolish way, babbling without substance.

clue.text: Middle of August taking afternoon tea and cake

indicators.note: to take something in is to hold it within, so one piece goes inside
the centre of a word is its middle letters only

explanation.surface: Afternoon tea and cake in the middle of August.
explanation.walkthrough: Afternoon tea reads as one phrase, but afternoon is its own abbreviation followed by tea.
explanation.definitionFit: A gateau is a rich layered cream cake, the French word for cake.
